name: Solana AI Trading Agent Workflow
goal: Build an autonomous AI agent that monitors Solana onchain data, makes trading decisions, and executes trades with MEV protection.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When multi-chain support is needed or QuickNode Yellowstone gRPC streaming is required for ultra-low-latency.

phases.phase_notes: Helius webhooks are the cleanest way to trigger agent logic on onchain events. Set up webhook subscriptions before building agent logic — the event model shapes everything downstream. Never use public RPCs for production agents.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: For cross-chain market data or when Birdeye pricing is a concern.

phases.phase_notes: Add Birdeye when the agent needs market data beyond raw transaction events — price signals, OHLCV, wallet P&L, trader intelligence. Helius covers onchain events; Birdeye covers market context.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When building a character-based social trading agent with persona requirements. Less production-stable than Vercel AI SDK.
When complex multi-step reasoning chains or Python-native tooling is required.

phases.phase_notes: Claude is the recommended LLM for complex trading reasoning. Use structured outputs to extract trading decisions from LLM responses — avoid parsing free text. Build the reasoning layer to be testable in isolation before connecting to live execution.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When upgrading from @solana/web3.js — @solana/kit is the official successor SDK and is required for modern Solana transaction construction. Pair with Turnkey for server-side key management. Note: @solana/web3.js v1 is maintenance-only; new Solana apps should use @solana/kit.

phases.phase_notes: Server-side wallet signing is a hard requirement for autonomous agents. NEVER use browser wallets or user-facing wallets for agent signing. Turnkey provides programmatic key management for server-side use. This is not optional.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When the agent needs direct AMM interactions or liquidity provisioning rather than swap aggregation.

phases.phase_notes: Jupiter is the default swap aggregator. For MEV-sensitive execution, combine Jupiter routing with Jito bundle submission — Jupiter handles route optimization, Jito handles submission priority.

Add Jito when competitive execution matters — e.g., arbitrage, high-frequency signals, or protecting against sandwich attacks. Jito bundle submission adds latency complexity. Build retry logic: bundle success rates are not 100%.

scale_overrides.production: Production trading agents at any meaningful volume need Jito. Build it in from the start rather than retrofitting.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: Simpler workflows with less complex retry requirements.
For very complex multi-step workflows requiring durable execution guarantees.

phases.phase_notes: Workflow orchestration adds durability to agent execution — retries, step visibility, failure handling. Worth adding from MVP for any production-bound agent. Debugging autonomous agents without execution traces is extremely difficult.

scale_overrides.production: Required. Production trading agents without durable orchestration will have unexplainable failures.

production_notes: Server-side wallet management (Turnkey) is a non-negotiable production requirement. Browser wallets in autonomous agents are a security failure mode.
Build a simulation/dry-run mode before connecting to live execution. Test every agent action in simulation before going live.
Implement spending limits and rate limiting for autonomous agents. An unconstrained agent can execute expensive actions at machine speed.
Helius rate limits matter at high frequency — plan your tier before launch, not after you hit the limit.
Jito bundle success rates vary. Build exponential backoff and alternative submission paths for production agents.
Agent memory design (how state is stored and retrieved) is as important as agent reasoning design. Plan it early.
tradeoffs: Helius + Jito adds infrastructure complexity but is required for competitive Solana execution.
Turnkey adds a server-side signing dependency — single point of failure if not architected with redundancy.
Python preferred if heavy ML/model work is needed; Node.js if JS-native tooling alignment is more important.
ElizaOS has stronger character/persona tooling but is less production-stable than Vercel AI SDK for trading agents.
anti_patterns: Using browser wallets or user-facing wallets for server-side agent signing.
Shipping without a simulation/dry-run mode — live trading bugs are financially expensive.
Skipping spending limits and rate limiting for autonomous execution.
Using public Solana RPCs instead of Helius — rate limits will fail under agent workload.
Not building retry logic for Jito bundle submission.

constraint_modifiers.modification: Server-side signing (Turnkey) is required. Never use browser wallets. Enforce spending limits and rate limiting.
Replace Vercel AI SDK with LangChain or direct Claude API. Replace Node.js orchestration with Python-native tools.
Jito MEV protection is less critical. Can use standard RPC submission via QuickNode instead.
Skip Jito and orchestration phases. Use Helius + Jupiter + Turnkey + Vercel AI SDK as the minimal viable stack.
